stem: 6 workers can paint a school building in 12 days. Working at the same rate, how many days would 8 workers take to paint the same building?
hints: More workers finish faster. When one amount goes up and the other goes down, it is an inverse proportion.
Find the total work in worker-days: 6 workers × 12 days.
6 × 12 gives the worker-days for the whole job. Share them among 8 workers by dividing by 8.

solution.methodName: Inverse proportion: find the total work, then divide

steps.action: Decide the type: more workers means fewer days. This is an inverse proportion.
steps.why: In an inverse proportion you multiply first, then divide. Cross-multiplying the usual way would give more days, which makes no sense.
A worker-day is one worker working for one day. The job always needs 72 of them, however many workers there are.

steps.action: Divide the total work by the new number of workers: 72 ÷ 8 = 9.

trapNotes.16 days: This treats it as a direct proportion: 12 × 8 ÷ 6 = 16. More workers should take fewer days, not more.
trapNotes.10 days: This subtracts: 2 more workers, so 2 fewer days (12 − 2). Multiply and divide instead of subtracting.
trapNotes.72 days: This is the total work, 6 × 12 = 72 worker-days. Divide it by 8 workers to get the number of days.
